title: Notes: Tab and Shift+Tab move only the bullet you are on
story: In Notes, Tab and Shift+Tab now move only the selected bullet or bullets, each with its own nested bullets. Shift+Tab puts the outdented bullet just after the bullet that held it, so the bullets that followed stay where they were; before, they ended up nested under it and a later Tab dragged them deeper. Tab on a first bullet no longer jumps out of the editor, and Shift+Tab on a top-level bullet still turns it into plain text.

checks.criterion: Tab on a middle bullet indents only it and its own nested bullets.
checks.steps: Open a note, type three bullets 'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma'. Put the caret on 'beta' and press Tab.
checks.expected: 'beta' moves under 'alpha'; 'gamma' stays at the top level.

checks.criterion: Shift+Tab on a nested bullet leaves the bullets below it at their level.
checks.steps: Make 'alpha' with two nested bullets 'beta' and 'gamma', then a top-level 'delta'. Put the caret on 'beta', press Shift+Tab, then press Tab.
checks.expected: After Shift+Tab, 'gamma' stays under 'alpha' and 'beta' sits between 'alpha' and 'delta'. After Tab, 'beta' is back under 'alpha' after 'gamma', and 'gamma' never went deeper.

checks.criterion: Tab on the first bullet keeps the cursor in the editor and changes nothing.
checks.steps: Type bullets 'alpha' and 'beta', put the caret on 'alpha', press Tab, then type 'x'.

checks.criterion: A selection over several bullets indents and outdents exactly those bullets.
checks.steps: Make 'alpha' with nested 'beta', 'gamma' and 'delta'. Select 'beta' through 'gamma' and press Shift+Tab.
checks.expected: 'beta' and 'gamma' go to the top level after 'alpha'; 'delta' stays under 'alpha'.
